title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 25
statement: A round table has radius \(4.\) Six rectangular place mats are placed on the table. Each place mat has width \(1\) and length \(x\) as shown. They are positioned so that each mat has two corners on the edge of the table, these two corners being end points of the same side of length \(x.\) Further, the mats are positioned so that the inner corners each touch an inner corner of an adjacent mat. What is \(x?\)

solutions.text:
Pick a mat with outer corners \(P\) and \(Q,\) and let \(R\) be the point on the circle diametrically opposite \(P.\) Then \(\triangle PQR\) is right-angled at \(Q\) with hypotenuse \(PR = 8.\)

The inner corners of adjacent mats meet in isosceles triangles with vertex angle \(120^\circ\) and sides \(x,\) whose base is \(\sqrt{3}\,x.\) Together with the two mat widths, \(QR = \sqrt{3}\,x + 2.\)

By the Pythagorean theorem, \[ \left(\sqrt{3}\,x + 2\right)^2 + x^2 = 64, \] which simplifies to \(x^2 + \sqrt{3}\,x - 15 = 0.\)

Taking the positive root, \[ x = \dfrac{3\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}}{2}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Take one mat with outer corners \(P, Q,\) and let \(R\) be the point of the circle opposite \(P,\) so \(\triangle PQR\) is right-angled with hypotenuse \(8\)
The inner corners meet in \(120^\circ\) isosceles triangles, giving \(QR = \sqrt{3}\,x + 2\)
